docs.title: frax: Fast Robot Kinematics and Dynamics in JAX
docs.text:
frax is a fast kinematics and dynamics library in pure Python, using JAX for JIT-compilation and automatic differentiation.

With frax, you can design high-performance inverse-kinematics and inverse-dynamics controllers at the speed of Pinocchio, ease of use of Python, and differentiation and parallelization-compatibility of MJX.

On CPU, you can expect compute times for typical controllers in the low microseconds range (~25-100 kHz), and on GPU or TPU, frax can compute dynamics terms at upwards of 100 million computations per second, depending on your batch size.

docs.title: New: Inverse kinematics and retargeting with frax.ik (at >100,000 FPS)
docs.text: frax 0.2.0 now includes new utilities for fast, flexible IK pipelines! For full details, check out the the frax.ik guide and the examples in examples/ik (humanoid retargeting, as well as interactive manipulator and quadruped IK demos).

docs.title: From PyPI
docs.text:
pip install "frax[ik]"

If you're getting started, frax[ik] will pull in all frax functionality, including the new IK logic. But if you just want the core kinematics/dynamics terms, or compatibility with older JAX (before 0.9.1), you can install frax directly.

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/StanfordASL/frax
cd frax
pip install -e ".[ik]"

If you're installing from source, I highly recommend using a uv-managed virtual environment. In this case, pip commands can be replaced with uv pip

For more fine-grained control over the JAX install for GPU/TPU, you can also use the [cuda12], [cuda13], or [tpu] tags.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
[!NOTE] Remember to install from source with the [examples] dependencies: pip install -e ".[examples]"

frax's "hello world": Compute your robot's mass matrix (AKA joint-space inertia matrix) 

import frax
import jax

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)  # Recommmended for high accuracy

robot = frax.Robot("path/to/your/robot.urdf")  # Or use a built-in model, e.g. frax.load_panda()
q = robot.default_configuration
M = robot.mass_matrix(q)
print(M)
For any operations with frax and jax more broadly, you should wrap your code in a jitted region, for instance, 
@jax.jit
def jit_mass_matrix(q_):
    return robot.mass_matrix(q_)

M = jit_mass_matrix(q)
print(M)
See the Performance Tips section below for more advice on making your code fast.

Many more kinematics and dynamics terms are available (joint/link/frame transforms and Jacobians, gravity vector, centrifugal/coriolis forces, and many other values relevant to robot control). We also provide Manipulator, Humanoid, and Quadruped classes for useful helper functions based on your robot's form-factor, and frax comes pre-loaded with the Franka Panda, Kuka iiwa, Unitree G1, and Unitree A2.

More advanced and interactive demos are included in the examples directory, as seen below

Examples of using frax for typical robot controllers: - Differential inverse kinematics: examples/control/diff_ik_demo.py - Operational space control: examples/control/osc_demo.py

When these scripts are launched in trajectory mode, you'll see the following sinusoidal tracking demo:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b471496-2124-4063-953a-d7f25776ed5b

This can also be launched in manual mode, for interactive mouse control of the target.

However, these controllers are fairly simple, and Pinocchio or MuJoCo could have been used to give the same Jacobians and inertial values. The real benefit of frax comes from the automatic differentiation through the kinematics and dynamics for flexible controller design with minimal manual Jacobian derivations. In the below demo (examples/control/oscbf_demo.py), I've reimplemented OSCBF, which uses JAX's autodiff under the hood to form the CBF constraints.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ea84ec0-6b67-40fd-a974-5850499df15d

Here, we're enforcing - Singularity avoidance - Joint limit avoidance - Collision avoidance with the floor - Collision avoidance with an external obstacle - Self-collision avoidance

... all with easy prototyping of the constraint design, in simple functions of the robot kinematics and dynamics (such as, robot.ee_manipulability_index(q) >= eps).

docs.title: Usage tips
docs.text:
• If you would like to use frax's collision methods, you must first define a spherized collision model of your robot (or, use our pre-built collision models for the Franka Panda/FR3, Unitree G1, and more). Check out this page for more info!
  • For now, if you have joints in your URDF that are not part of the primary kinematic chain/tree being controlled (for instance, gripper joints), please set these as fixed so that they can be ignored, and so their child links' inertias can be fused into the parent. In the future, we will allow for fixing joints programmatically.
  • Free-floating bases with a quaternion rotation representation follow MuJoCo's convention: q = [position, WXYZ quaternion, joints] and v = [world-frame linear velocity, body-frame angular velocity, joint velocities]. The original implementation of frax used 6 "virtual joints" (3 prismatic, 3 revolute) to represent a floating base, in which case nq = nv and q_dot = v. However, the intrinsic Euler XYZ rotation representation can suffer from singularities / gimbal lock.
  • If working with quaternions, use robot.integrate(q, v, dt) rather than q + v * dt, and if you differentiate a function f(q) with autodiff, map the result back to velocity space with jax.jacobian(f)(q) @ robot.velocity_to_qdot_map(q).

docs.title: Performance tips
docs.text:
• If you're not planning on using frax.ik and only need fast dynamics on CPU, I recommend JAX version 0.4.30. This is due to a degradation in the XLA compiler performance in recent JAX versions, but the JAX/XLA team is currently working on addressing this: see https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/26021
  • If you're running on CPU, take advantage of double precision with jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True) or by setting the environment variable JAX_ENABLE_X64=True. On GPU, this is a more nuanced decision. Generally, running in double precision on GPU will lead to about a 2-6x slowdown, depending on your batch size, because GPUs are so well-suited for single-precision operations. This choice will be application-dependent -- you might need high precision, or maybe you can get away with being a little less precise.
  • I've also found that for typical CPU workflows with frax, it's better to configure JAX/XLA to run on a single thread. Generally, for robot controller design, the matrices involved are not quite large enough to require multithreading (unless you are doing something more parallelizable like MPPI). In this case, restricting it to a single thread can improve performance and also make it easier to share CPU resources across processes (multiple ROS nodes, for instance). You can use source scripts/setup_cpu_env.sh to load my recommended config, or feel free to modify as needed.
  • If you only need to solve for the dynamics of one robot instance, and you have a GPU on your computer, it will be significantly faster to use CPU. To force CPU usage, use jax.config.update("jax_platforms", "cpu") or set the environment variable JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu.
  • For certain batched operations, it often is fastest to parallelize across multiple CPU devices, rather than running on GPU. Check out how we handle batched dataset retargeting across multiple CPU devices in frax.ik!
  • frax by default does not wrap every method with a @jax.jit decorator. When calling any JAX code, add a JIT decorator to the top-most function call to ensure the best performance.
  • If you have any code that is outside of a jitted region, use numpy operations and arrays. Inside a jitted region, use jax.numpy.

For general advice on JAX, check out the quickstart guide and the sharp bits.

docs.title: New, breaking changes:
docs.text:
• I recently improved the handling of free-floating joints and added a position + WXYZ quaternion representation (following MuJoCo) rather than just position + intrinsic Euler XYZ. This should lead to fewer issues with gimbal lock, but I needed to update some terminology now that nq != nv. For instance:
  • Joint limits are specified now only in terms of the actuated joints
  • Terms like num_joints are deprecated in favor of nq and nv
  • I've updated the Unitree G1's collision model: there are now more collision bodies, more self-collision pairs, and better contact geometry at the feet. This new model is better for the retargeting in frax.ik.
  • The convention for fext has changed slightly in forward_dynamics, for the better. Previously, this was poorly documented and untested, and had an uncommon frame convention. Now, it uses a more intuitive convention: wrenches are applied at the link CoM frame, with axes aligned with the world frame.

I'll update this list if more changes come up.

docs.title: TODOs / upcoming features
docs.text:
frax is (by design) more minimal than other libraries -- resulting in high performance on the restricted setting of interest. But, there are a few more features I'd like to add in the future:

  • Add MJCF support
  • Add support for collision primitives other than just spheres
  • Analytical Jacobians of forward/inverse dynamics (see: Pinocchio)

The following features are unplanned: - Closed kinematic chains - Joint types other than revolute, prismatic, fixed, or free-floating

docs.title: Inverse kinematics and retargeting with frax.ik
docs.text:
frax.ik is a differential IK library, akin to mink and pink, but faster, compatible with automatic differentiation, and with more reliable constraint enforcement.

frax.ik is great for both online and offline IK problems. For example, applications include:

  • Online: Real-time (>1,000 Hz) velocity control of robot manipulators, online teleoperation and retargeting of humanoid robots
  • Offline: Batch processing and retargeting of trajectories and human motion data (>100,000 Hz)

frax.ik uses ElastiQP as the underlying QP solver for each differential IK step. This solver is always feasible, in the sense that it adds an (implicit) l1 relaxation on every inequality constraint. Check out the paper for more details!

docs.text: [!NOTE] Remember to install from source with the [examples] dependencies: pip install -e ".[examples]"

docs.title: Humanoid Retargeting
docs.text: frax.ik can churn through retargeting problems at extreme speeds (>100,000 FPS). For comparison, GMR's stated number is 70 FPS (on a threadripper, too).

docs.title: LAFAN1: Retarget the entire dataset in 4 seconds on CPU:
docs.text:
LAFAN1 is a great place to get started with humanoid retargeting. The dataset (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) is around 150 MB in size, and frax.ik processes it quickly (at over 100,000 FPS)

# If you haven't downloaded the dataset yet:
# python examples/ik/lafan1/download.py

python examples/ik/lafan1/retarget.py

(Timing numbers are from a i9-14900KF CPU. If you add the --self-collision-avoidance flag, it takes around 7 seconds. On my i7 laptop, it takes around 10 seconds)

Once that's done, run the following to take a look at the retargeted results in a viser viewer!

python examples/ik/lafan1/view.py

docs.title: BONES-SEED
docs.text:
To fetch the data for BONES-SEED, you'll need to first agree to some terms and conditions: see the HuggingFace page for more details and instructions.

This dataset is significantly larger than LAFAN1 (>100 GB!), and it is a much higher framerate. Processing the full set takes roughly 1 hour on my desktop. If you've got the storage space on your computer, and don't mind a short wait, download the dataset and then run the following:

python examples/ik/bones_seed/retarget.py

As with the LAFAN1 demo, we have a script to show the results in a viser viewer:

python examples/ik/bones_seed/view.py

Currently, all humanoid examples are configured to use the Unitree G1, which is built-in to frax. If you would like to use a new robot, you'll need a URDF and a collision model: see our other docs for more details.

docs.title: General IK problems
docs.text:
The best place to get started with frax.ik is in examples/ik/panda_interactive.py. Check out this file for a quick-start guide to how to define a set of IK tasks and constraints, and run the script to open up an interactive viewer for end-effector tracking!

python examples/ik/panda_interactive.py

Another interactive example is available in examples/ik/a2_interactive.py (quadruped IK with adjustable base pose and feet positions)

python examples/ik/a2_interactive.py

We also have a collision avoidance demo where a Panda tracks a pre-set trajectory and we enforce collision avoidance to an (interactive) external obstacle:

python examples/ik/panda_obstacle.py

For a more advanced example, we have a demo of how to set up a global IK problem with multiple samples parallelized across CPU devices:

python examples/ik/parallel_global_ik.py

docs.title: Modeling collision geometry for a new robot in frax
docs.text:
frax's kinematics and dynamics already supports most robots you can load with a URDF (MJCF support is pending).

But, if you would like to use frax's collision / self-collision modeling, you'll need to add a spherized collision model and define self-collision pairs.

Currently, frax contains tuned collision models for the following: - Franka Panda / FR3 - Unitree G1

There are a few tools out there to automatically spherize your robot geometry, for instance, foam or ballpark, but I prefer to hand-design these collision geometries with a tool like bubblify. It takes a short time to design a good collision model, but once this is done well, you don't have to worry about it again.

Here is a walkthrough of the steps I took to add the Franka Panda:

docs.title: 1. Find a good URDF with "accurate" inertial information.
docs.text:
This can be harder than you would expect for many robots. The best place to search is usually the official _description repo (for instance, franka_description), and building the URDF yourself.

Some alternative methods to this are: - Searching GitHub for "your_robot" with extension ".urdf". If it's a common robot, someone's probably uploaded the URDF already. But be warned that the inertial properties could be wrong - Using robot_descriptions if your robot is supported

docs.title: 2. Create a collision model
docs.text: To do this with bubblify (my preferred method), - Install bubblify either from source or with pip (see the repo for details) - Load your robot with bubblify --urdf_path path/to/your/robot.urdf - Add spheres interactively to each link. Tips for best performance with frax: minimize the maximum amount of spheres on any one link, and try to strike a good balance between number of spheres, and how tighly you represent the geometry. - Your model will look something like this when you're done:

docs.title: 3. Create a self-collision model
docs.text:
Now, given the spheres from the collision model, we'll define self-collision pairs to pay attention to. This could be an exhaustive list of every pair of spheres on the model, but this would be needlessly complex for most practical situations.

An example of how to define these pairs is located in frax/robots/franka_panda.py -- in general, you'll specify the link name and sphere index for both spheres, as well as an optional tolerance/inflation factor.

Alternatively, you can define the pairs by link, with frax.utils.collision_utils.link_pairs_to_sc_data: every sphere on one link is checked against every sphere on the other. This checks more pairs, but the pairs stay valid when you edit the spheres. See frax/robots/unitree_g1.py for an example.

docs.title: 4. Verify
docs.text:
Now, check that the collision model looks correct once it's loaded into frax. There's an example script at scripts/visualize_collision_model.py which will bring up the following, for the Panda:

The spheres associated with the self-collision model are indicated in red (with lines to denote the collision pairs), and standard collision spheres in yellow.

Note that it is perfectly fine to have a self-collision model which is simplified from the full-body collision model. For instance, with the Panda, we create self-collision pairs with the central sphere on the end-effector with a tolerance to "inflate" this central EE sphere so that the full EE is covered. This significantly reduces the number of pairs that we need to check, while only introducing slightly more conservative behavior when near self-collision.

@jax.tree_util.register_static
class Humanoid(Robot):
    """Humanoid kinematics and dynamics

    Args:
        urdf_filename (str): Path to the URDF file to load
        left_hand_parent_joint_name (str): Name of the left hand EE's parent joint
        right_hand_parent_joint_name (str): Name of the right hand EE's parent joint
        left_foot_parent_joint_name (str): Name of the left foot EE's parent joint
        right_foot_parent_joint_name (str): Name of the right foot EE's parent joint
        left_hand_ee_offset (Optional[ArrayLike]): Transformation matrix specifying the left hand EE
            offset from the parent joint frame. Defaults to None.
        right_hand_ee_offset (Optional[ArrayLike]): Transformation matrix specifying the right hand EE
            offset from the parent joint frame. Defaults to None.
        left_foot_ee_offset (Optional[ArrayLike]): Transformation matrix specifying the left foot EE
            offset from the parent joint frame. Defaults to None.
        right_foot_ee_offset (Optional[ArrayLike]): Transformation matrix specifying the right foot EE
            offset from the parent joint frame. Defaults to None.
        collision_data (Optional[dict]): Collision information. Contains info
            on body/root collision data, as well as self-collision pairs.
            See collision_utils for more detail. Defaults to None.
        joint_ordering (Optional[list[str]]): A specific joint ordering to use.
            Defaults to None (infer ordering from URDF)
        floating_base (Optional[str]): How to model the free-floating base: None (fixed base),
            "quaternion", or "euler". See Robot for details. Defaults to "quaternion".
        default_configuration (Optional[ArrayLike]): The default configuration, shape (nq,).
            See Robot for details. Defaults to None (identity base pose, all joints at zero)
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        urdf_filename,
        left_hand_parent_joint_name: str,
        right_hand_parent_joint_name: str,
        left_foot_parent_joint_name: str,
        right_foot_parent_joint_name: str,
        left_hand_ee_offset: ArrayLike | None = None,
        right_hand_ee_offset: ArrayLike | None = None,
        left_foot_ee_offset: ArrayLike | None = None,
        right_foot_ee_offset: ArrayLike | None = None,
        collision_data: dict | None = None,
        joint_ordering: list[str] | None = None,
        floating_base: str | None = "quaternion",
        default_configuration: ArrayLike | None = None,
    ):
        super().__init__(
            urdf_filename,
            collision_data,
            joint_ordering,
            floating_base,
            default_configuration,
        )

        self.left_hand_parent_chain = np.flatnonzero(
            self.ancestor_mask[self.joint_name_to_index[left_hand_parent_joint_name]]
        )
        self.right_hand_parent_chain = np.flatnonzero(
            self.ancestor_mask[self.joint_name_to_index[right_hand_parent_joint_name]]
        )
        self.left_foot_parent_chain = np.flatnonzero(
            self.ancestor_mask[self.joint_name_to_index[left_foot_parent_joint_name]]
        )
        self.right_foot_parent_chain = np.flatnonzero(
            self.ancestor_mask[self.joint_name_to_index[right_foot_parent_joint_name]]
        )

        if left_hand_ee_offset is None:
            self.left_hand_ee_offset = np.eye(4)
        else:
            left_hand_ee_offset = np.asarray(left_hand_ee_offset, dtype=float)
            assert left_hand_ee_offset.shape == (4, 4)
            self.left_hand_ee_offset = left_hand_ee_offset

        if right_hand_ee_offset is None:
            self.right_hand_ee_offset = np.eye(4)
        else:
            right_hand_ee_offset = np.asarray(right_hand_ee_offset, dtype=float)
            assert right_hand_ee_offset.shape == (4, 4)
            self.right_hand_ee_offset = right_hand_ee_offset

        if left_foot_ee_offset is None:
            self.left_foot_ee_offset = np.eye(4)
        else:
            left_foot_ee_offset = np.asarray(left_foot_ee_offset, dtype=float)
            assert left_foot_ee_offset.shape == (4, 4)
            self.left_foot_ee_offset = left_foot_ee_offset

        if right_foot_ee_offset is None:
            self.right_foot_ee_offset = np.eye(4)
        else:
            right_foot_ee_offset = np.asarray(right_foot_ee_offset, dtype=float)
            assert right_foot_ee_offset.shape == (4, 4)
            self.right_foot_ee_offset = right_foot_ee_offset

    # HANDS AND FEET TRANSFORMS

    def left_hand_transform(self, q: Array) -> Array:
        """Transformation matrix of the left hand (w.r.t world), shape (4, 4)"""
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._left_hand_transform(transforms)

    def _left_hand_transform(self, joint_transforms: Array) -> Array:
        return self._frame_transform(
            joint_transforms, self.left_hand_ee_offset, self.left_hand_parent_chain[-1]
        )

    def right_hand_transform(self, q: Array) -> Array:
        """Transformation matrix of the right hand (w.r.t world), shape (4, 4)"""
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._right_hand_transform(transforms)

    def _right_hand_transform(self, joint_transforms: Array) -> Array:
        return self._frame_transform(
            joint_transforms,
            self.right_hand_ee_offset,
            self.right_hand_parent_chain[-1],
        )

    def left_foot_transform(self, q: Array) -> Array:
        """Transformation matrix of the left foot (w.r.t world), shape (4, 4)"""
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._left_foot_transform(transforms)

    def _left_foot_transform(self, joint_transforms: Array) -> Array:
        return self._frame_transform(
            joint_transforms, self.left_foot_ee_offset, self.left_foot_parent_chain[-1]
        )

    def right_foot_transform(self, q: Array) -> Array:
        """Transformation matrix of the right foot (w.r.t world), shape (4, 4)"""
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._right_foot_transform(transforms)

    def _right_foot_transform(self, joint_transforms: Array) -> Array:
        return self._frame_transform(
            joint_transforms,
            self.right_foot_ee_offset,
            self.right_foot_parent_chain[-1],
        )

    # HANDS AND FEET JACOBIANS

    def left_hand_jacobian(self, q: Array) -> Array:
        """Left hand Jacobian (w.r.t world), [Jv; Jw], shape (6, nv)"""
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._left_hand_jacobian(transforms)

    def _left_hand_jacobian(self, joint_transforms: Array):
        return self._frame_jacobian(
            joint_transforms, self.left_hand_ee_offset, self.left_hand_parent_chain
        )

    def left_hand_jacobian_and_derivative(
        self, q: Array, v: Array
    ) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Left hand Jacobian and its time derivative (w.r.t world), both of shape (6, nv)"""
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._left_hand_jacobian_and_derivative(v, transforms)

    def _left_hand_jacobian_and_derivative(
        self, v: Array, joint_transforms: Array
    ) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        return self._frame_jacobian_and_derivative(
            v, joint_transforms, self.left_hand_ee_offset, self.left_hand_parent_chain
        )

    def right_hand_jacobian(self, q: Array) -> Array:
        """Right hand Jacobian (w.r.t world), [Jv; Jw], shape (6, nv)"""
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._right_hand_jacobian(transforms)

    def _right_hand_jacobian(self, joint_transforms: Array):
        return self._frame_jacobian(
            joint_transforms, self.right_hand_ee_offset, self.right_hand_parent_chain
        )

    def right_hand_jacobian_and_derivative(
        self, q: Array, v: Array
    ) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Right hand Jacobian and its time derivative (w.r.t world), both of shape (6, nv)"""
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._right_hand_jacobian_and_derivative(v, transforms)

    def _right_hand_jacobian_and_derivative(
        self, v: Array, joint_transforms: Array
    ) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        return self._frame_jacobian_and_derivative(
            v,
            joint_transforms,
            self.right_hand_ee_offset,
            self.right_hand_parent_chain,
        )

    def left_foot_jacobian(self, q: Array) -> Array:
        """Left foot Jacobian (w.r.t world), [Jv; Jw], shape (6, nv)"""
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._left_foot_jacobian(transforms)

def integrate(self, q: Array, v: Array, dt: float) -> Array:
    """Integrates a configuration forward in time with a constant velocity

    Args:
        q (Array): Configuration, shape (nq,)
        v (Array): Velocity, shape (nv,)
        dt (float): Timestep

    Returns:
        Array: New configuration, shape (nq,)
    """
    if not self.is_quaternion_base:
        return q + v * dt
    pos = q[:3] + v[:3] * dt
    quat = quat_wxyz_multiply(q[3:7], quat_wxyz_exp(v[3:6] * dt))
    quat = quat / jnp.linalg.norm(quat)
    q_act = q[7:] + v[6:] * dt
    return jnp.concatenate([pos, quat, q_act])

def difference(self, q0: Array, q1: Array) -> Array:
    """Computes the velocity which takes q0 to q1 in unit time
    (inverse of integrate)

    Args:
        q0 (Array): Starting configuration, shape (nq,)
        q1 (Array): Ending configuration, shape (nq,)

    Returns:
        Array: Velocity, shape (nv,)
    """
    if not self.is_quaternion_base:
        return q1 - q0
    quat_rel = quat_wxyz_multiply(quat_wxyz_conjugate(q0[3:7]), q1[3:7])
    return jnp.concatenate(
        [q1[:3] - q0[:3], quat_wxyz_log(quat_rel), q1[7:] - q0[7:]]
    )

def velocity_to_qdot_map(self, q: Array) -> Array:
    """Matrix E(q) mapping velocities to the time derivative of the configuration:
    q_dot = E(q) @ v

    This is useful when combining autodiff w.r.t. q with velocities, e.g.
    dh/dt = (dh/dq) @ E(q) @ v. When nq == nv, this is the identity.

    Args:
        q (Array): Configuration, shape (nq,)

    Returns:
        Array: Velocity map, shape (nq, nv)
    """
    if not self.is_quaternion_base:
        return jnp.eye(self.nv)
    w, x, y, z = q[3:7]
    # q_dot = 0.5 * quat * [0, omega_body] (quaternion multiplication)
    quat_map = 0.5 * jnp.array([[-x, -y, -z], [w, -z, y], [z, w, -x], [-y, x, w]])
    E = jnp.zeros((self.nq, self.nv))
    E = E.at[:3, :3].set(jnp.eye(3))
    E = E.at[3:7, 3:6].set(quat_map)
    E = E.at[7:, 6:].set(jnp.eye(self.num_actuated_joints))
    return E

docs.title: Inverse Kinematics
docs.text:
Differential IK

min sum_tasks || weight * (J v - v_des) ||^2 + (reg + lam) * ||v||^2 s.t. A v == b; G v <= h

i.e. - Minimimize the weighted task velocity error, plus regularization and damping terms for stability - Subject to a set of equality and inequality constraints

Note that since we use ElastiQP as our solver, inequality constraints are automatically (and efficiently) relaxed with an L1 penalty term. These constraints are held exactly when the problem is feasible, and only relaxed when the problem is infeasible*

*See the ElastiQP paper for more details, and more precise conditions on relaxation and when this occurs

Equality constraints are still held as hard constraints with ElastiQP, unless explicitly posed as an elastic equality. In this case, the equality is converted to a pair of opposing elastic inequalities.

Differential IK tasks

Notes: - Tasks operate on the velocity level, as opposed to a delta-q. - In general, a task has a least-squares structure || weight * (J v - v_des) ||^2

IK constraints

Notes: - We use ElastiQP for our solver, which allows us to use efficient elastic inequality constraints, and hard equalities (where applicable) - Each inequality has an L1 relaxation with associated penalty w, typically left at a default high value like 1e6, though this can be tuned on a per-task basis. If this penalty is greater than the optimal dual multiplier for a feasible problem, the relaxation is exact - For tuning gains, ensure that gain * dt <= 1 to avoid overshoot - Since this solver operates on generalized velocities, all inequalities deal with v rather than a delta q. This is slightly different from other diff IK libraries like pink or mink

Online and offline motion retargeting

Global IK with multi-start SQP

Note: for continuous motion control, you should probably stick to differential IK. Global IK is useful for if instantaneous jumps are acceptable: for instance, finding a configuration that achieves a desired initial or goal pose, without worrying about continuity from your current state.

@jax.tree_util.register_static
class DiffIKSolver:
    """Differential IK with ElastiQP

    Args:
        robot (Robot): Robot model
        tasks (Sequence[Task]): Tracking tasks
        constraints (Sequence[InequalityConstraint | EqualityConstraint]):
            Constraints. Defaults to an empty tuple (unconstrained)
        regularization (ArrayLike): Tikhonov regularization on v,
            scalar or shape (nv,). Defaults to 1e-8
        damping (float): Levenberg-Marquardt damping, per unit of task cost.
            Defaults to 0.0 (no damping)
        solver_tol (float): QP solver tolerance. Defaults to 1e-5
        warm_start (bool): Whether to warm-start each QP from the previous
            solution. Defaults to True.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        robot: Robot,
        tasks: Sequence[Task],
        constraints: Sequence[InequalityConstraint | EqualityConstraint] = (),
        regularization: ArrayLike = 1e-8,
        damping: float = 0.0,
        solver_tol: float = 1e-5,
        warm_start: bool = True,
    ):
        assert len(tasks) > 0
        assert damping >= 0
        self.robot = robot
        self.tasks = tuple(tasks)
        self.constraints = tuple(constraints)
        self.regularization = np.broadcast_to(
            np.asarray(regularization, dtype=float), (robot.nv,)
        ).copy()
        self.damping = damping
        self.solver_tol = solver_tol
        self.warm_start = warm_start
        self.max_gain = _max_gain(self.tasks + self.constraints)
        for c in self.constraints:
            assert isinstance(c, InequalityConstraint | EqualityConstraint), (
                f"{type(c).__name__} is neither an InequalityConstraint nor an "
                + "EqualityConstraint"
            )
        for term in self.tasks + self.constraints:
            assert term.robot is robot, (
                f"{type(term).__name__} was built for a different robot than the solver's"
            )
        self.inequalities = tuple(
            c for c in self.constraints if isinstance(c, InequalityConstraint)
        )
        self.equalities = tuple(
            c for c in self.constraints if isinstance(c, EqualityConstraint)
        )
        self.n_eq = sum(c.num_rows for c in self.equalities)

        def penalties(c):
            return np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(c.penalty, dtype=float), (c.num_rows,))

        self.penalty = np.concatenate(
            [penalties(c) for c in self.inequalities] + [np.zeros(0)]
        )
        self.n_ineq = len(self.penalty)

    def init(self, q0: Array) -> SolverState:
        nv = self.robot.nv
        qp_warm_start = (jnp.zeros(nv), jnp.zeros(self.n_eq), jnp.zeros(self.n_ineq))
        q = jnp.asarray(q0, dtype=jnp.float64)  # float64 for elastiqp
        return SolverState(q=q, qp_warm_start=qp_warm_start)

    def _qp(self, q: Array, ref: Any):
        """The diff IK QP at q, and the cost of q

        Returns:
            tuple: P, c, G, h, A, b (A and b are None if there are no hard
                equalities), and the cost of q (the QP objective at v = 0)
        """
        robot = self.robot
        assert q.shape == (robot.nq,), f"q has shape {q.shape}, expected ({robot.nq},)"
        Js, v_des, ws = zip(*(task.linearize(q, ref) for task in self.tasks))
        w = jnp.concatenate(ws)
        WJ = w[:, None] * jnp.concatenate(Js)
        w_v_des = w * jnp.concatenate(v_des)
        task_error = jnp.sum(w_v_des**2)
        P = WJ.T @ WJ + jnp.diag(self.regularization + self.damping * task_error)
        c = -w_v_des @ WJ

        Gs, hs = [jnp.zeros((0, robot.nv))], [jnp.zeros(0)]
        for con in self.inequalities:
            G, h = con.rows(q, ref)
            Gs.append(G)
            hs.append(h)
        G = jnp.concatenate(Gs)
        h = jnp.concatenate(hs)
        cost = task_error + jnp.maximum(-h, 0.0) @ self.penalty

        A = b = None
        if self.equalities:
            As, bs = zip(*(con.rows(q, ref) for con in self.equalities))
            A = jnp.concatenate(As)
            b = jnp.concatenate(bs)
            # Hard equalities have no penalty, so their residual |A 0 - b| is
            # weighted like a default elastic row's
            cost += DEFAULT_PENALTY * jnp.sum(jnp.abs(b))
        return P, c, G, h, A, b, cost

    def cost(self, q: Array, ref: Any) -> Array:
        """The cost of q: the QP objective at v = 0 (if the robot doesn't move),
        for the given reference data"""
        *_, cost = self._qp(q, ref)
        return cost

    def solve(
        self, q: Array, ref: Any, qp_warm_start: tuple[Array, Array, Array]
    ) -> tuple[Array, tuple[Array, Array, Array], SolverInfo]:
        """Solve the diff IK QP

        Args:
            q (Array): Configuration, shape (nq,)
            ref (Any): Per-step reference data (any pytree)
            qp_warm_start (tuple[Array, Array, Array]): QP warm start (x, y, z)

        Returns:
            v (Array): Generalized velocity, shape (nv,)
            qp_warm_start (tuple[Array, Array, Array]): QP solution (x, y, z),
                to warm-start the next QP
            info (SolverInfo): Solver info, with the cost of q
        """
        P, c, G, h, A, b, cost = self._qp(q, ref)
        result = elastiqp.jax.solve(
            P,
            c,
            G,
            h,
            penalty=self.penalty,
            A=A,
            b=b,
            eps_abs=self.solver_tol,
            warm_start=qp_warm_start if self.warm_start else None,
        )
        info = SolverInfo(result.iters, result.converged, cost)
        return result.x, (result.x, result.y, result.z), info

    def step(
        self, state: SolverState, ref: Any, dt: float
    ) -> tuple[SolverState, Array, SolverInfo]:
        """One diff IK step

        Args:
            state (SolverState): Current state
            ref (Any): Per-step reference data (any pytree)
            dt (float): Timestep

        Returns:
            state (SolverState): New state
            v (Array): Generalized velocity, shape (nv,)
            info (SolverInfo): Solver info
        """
        v, qp_warm_start, info = self.solve(state.q, ref, state.qp_warm_start)
        q = self.robot.integrate(state.q, v, dt)
        return SolverState(q=q, qp_warm_start=qp_warm_start), v, info

    def converge(
        self, state: SolverState, ref: Any, max_iters: int, dt_max: float, tol: float
    ) -> tuple[SolverState, Array]:
        """Run differential IK until convergence

        Note: This method should generally only be called as a component of a
        global IK pipeline, or at initialization of a solver. During online
        operation, or sequential calls in an offline pipeline, generally
        only a single diff IK step() should be taken.

        Args:
            state (SolverState): Initial state
            ref (Any): Reference data (any pytree)
            max_iters (int): Maximum iterations
            dt_max (float): Largest stepsize
            tol (float): Convergence tolerance on max |v|

        Returns:
            state (SolverState): Converged state
            iters (Array): Number of iterations
        """
        state, ref = jax.lax.stop_gradient((state, ref))
        robot = self.robot
        v, qp_warm_start, info = self.solve(state.q, ref, state.qp_warm_start)
        dt_min = MIN_STEP_RATIO * dt_max

        def cond(carry):
            *_, i, done = carry
            return ~done & (i < max_iters)

        def body(carry):
            q, v, qp_warm_start, cost, dt, i, _ = carry
            q_new = robot.integrate(q, v, dt)
            v_new, qp_warm_start_new, info = self.solve(q_new, ref, qp_warm_start)
            # Accept if the step lowers the cost
            accept = info.cost < cost
            q, v, qp_warm_start, cost = jax.tree.map(
                lambda new, old: jnp.where(accept, new, old),
                (q_new, v_new, qp_warm_start_new, info.cost),
                (q, v, qp_warm_start, cost),
            )
            # If accepted, double dt, otherwise halve it
            dt = jnp.where(accept, jnp.minimum(2.0 * dt, dt_max), 0.5 * dt)
            # Stopping condition on the max |v| or on a minimum dt
            done = (accept & (jnp.max(jnp.abs(v)) <= tol)) | (dt < dt_min)
            return q, v, qp_warm_start, cost, dt, i + 1, done

        carry = (
            state.q,
            v,
            qp_warm_start,
            info.cost,
            jnp.asarray(dt_max, dtype=state.q.dtype),
            0,
            jnp.max(jnp.abs(v)) <= tol,
        )
        q, _, qp_warm_start, _, _, iters, _ = jax.lax.while_loop(cond, body, carry)
        return SolverState(q=q, qp_warm_start=qp_warm_start), iters

        weight: ArrayLike = 1.0,

        self.num_rows = num_rows

class JointTask(Task):
    """Track a joint-space task

    Note: this is currently configured to only deal with actuated
    joints. For free-floating bases, use a FrameTask

    Args:
        robot (Robot): Robot model
        idxs (ArrayLike): Indices into v to track
        ref_key (str): Reference key for the targets, shape (len(idxs),)
        gain (ArrayLike): Scalar or per-joint gain (1/s)
        weight (ArrayLike): Scalar or per-joint weight
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        robot: Robot,
        idxs: ArrayLike,
        ref_key: str,
        gain: ArrayLike = 1.0,
        weight: ArrayLike = 1.0,
    ):
        self.robot = robot
        self.idxs = np.asarray(idxs)
        v_to_q = robot.velocity_to_configuration_index
        assert all(int(i) in v_to_q for i in self.idxs), (
            "JointTask entries must have q_dot = v (not a quaternion base's orientation)"
        )
        self.q_idxs = np.array([v_to_q[int(i)] for i in self.idxs], dtype=int)
        self.J = np.eye(robot.nv)[self.idxs]
        self.ref_key = ref_key
        self.num_rows = len(self.idxs)
        self.gain = _per_row(gain, self.num_rows)
        self.weight = _per_row(weight, self.num_rows)

    def linearize(self, q, ref):
        e = q[self.q_idxs] - ref[self.ref_key]
        return self.J, -self.gain * e, self.weight

@jax.tree_util.register_static
class FrameTask(_PoseTask):
    """Track world-frame positions and/or orientations of joint frames

    Args:
        robot (Robot): Robot model
        joints (ArrayLike): Indices of the tracked joints, shape (n,)
        gain_pos, gain_rot (ArrayLike): Scalar or per-frame gains (1/s)
        weight_pos, weight_rot (ArrayLike): Scalar or per-frame weights
        pos_key (str | None): Reference key for target positions, shape (n, 3).
            None to not track position
        rot_key (str | None): Reference key for target rotation matrices,
            shape (n, 3, 3). None to not track rotation
        offsets (ArrayLike | None): Tracked frames in their joint frames, shape
            (4, 4) or (n, 4, 4). Defaults to None (identity)
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        robot: Robot,
        joints: ArrayLike,
        gain_pos: ArrayLike = 1.0,
        gain_rot: ArrayLike = 1.0,
        weight_pos: ArrayLike = 1.0,
        weight_rot: ArrayLike = 1.0,
        pos_key: str | None = "frame_pos",
        rot_key: str | None = "frame_rmat",
        offsets: ArrayLike | None = None,
    ):
        self.joints = np.asarray(joints)
        n = len(self.joints)
        super().__init__(
            robot, n, gain_pos, gain_rot, weight_pos, weight_rot, pos_key, rot_key
        )
        if offsets is not None:
            offsets = np.broadcast_to(
                np.asarray(offsets, dtype=float), (n, 4, 4)
            ).copy()
        self.offsets = offsets

    def linearize(self, q, ref):
        tfs = self.robot.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        Jv, Jw = self.robot._joint_jacobians(tfs)
        tfs, Jv, Jw = tfs[self.joints], Jv[self.joints], Jw[self.joints]
        if self.offsets is not None:
            tfs, Jv, Jw = offset_transforms_and_jacobians(tfs, Jv, Jw, self.offsets)
        return self._pose_rows(tfs, jnp.concatenate([Jv, Jw], axis=1), ref)

@jax.tree_util.register_static
class JointLimits(InequalityConstraint):
    """Joint position and velocity limits on the actuated joint velocities

        max(v_min, gain * (q_min - q)) <= v <= min(v_max, gain * (q_max - q))

    Limits default to "robot" to use the robot's own actuated joint position/
    velocity limits, but you can also pass None (no limit) or an array of
    custom limits.

    Currently, limits on floating bases are not implemented.

    Args:
        robot (Robot): The frax robot model
        q_min (ArrayLike | str | None): Lower position limits, shape (num_actuated,).
            Defaults to robot.actuated_joint_lower_limits
        q_max (ArrayLike | str | None): Upper position limits, shape (num_actuated,).
            Defaults to robot.actuated_joint_upper_limits
        v_max (ArrayLike | str | None): Upper velocity limits, shape (num_actuated,).
            Defaults to robot.actuated_joint_max_velocities
        v_min (ArrayLike | str | None): Lower velocity limits, shape (num_actuated,).
            Defaults to -v_max
        gain (float): CBF gain (1/s): how fast the position limits may be approached
        penalty (float): Relaxation penalty
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        robot: Robot,
        q_min: ArrayLike | Literal["robot"] | None = "robot",
        q_max: ArrayLike | Literal["robot"] | None = "robot",
        v_max: ArrayLike | Literal["robot"] | None = "robot",
        v_min: ArrayLike | Literal["robot"] | None = "robot",
        gain: float = 10.0,
        penalty: float = DEFAULT_PENALTY,
    ):
        assert gain > 0
        self.robot = robot
        n = robot.nv - robot.nv_floating  # Actuated joints
        self.q_min = _resolve_limits(q_min, robot.actuated_joint_lower_limits, n, -1)
        self.q_max = _resolve_limits(q_max, robot.actuated_joint_upper_limits, n, 1)
        self.v_max = _resolve_limits(v_max, robot.actuated_joint_max_velocities, n, 1)
        self.v_min = _resolve_limits(v_min, -self.v_max, n, -1)
        self.upper_idxs = np.flatnonzero(
            np.isfinite(self.q_max) | np.isfinite(self.v_max)
        )
        self.lower_idxs = np.flatnonzero(
            np.isfinite(self.q_min) | np.isfinite(self.v_min)
        )
        I = np.eye(n)
        G = np.vstack([I[self.upper_idxs], -I[self.lower_idxs]])
        self.num_rows = G.shape[0]
        assert self.num_rows > 0
        # Zero columns for the floating base
        self.G = np.hstack([np.zeros((self.num_rows, robot.nv_floating)), G])
        self.gain = gain
        self.penalty = penalty

    def rows(self, q, ref):
        pos = q[self.robot.nq_floating :]
        up, lo = self.upper_idxs, self.lower_idxs
        upper = jnp.minimum(self.v_max[up], self.gain * (self.q_max[up] - pos[up]))
        lower = jnp.maximum(self.v_min[lo], self.gain * (self.q_min[lo] - pos[lo]))
        return self.G, jnp.concatenate([upper, -lower])

@jax.tree_util.register_static
class ObstacleConstraint(_SphereConstraint):
    """Sphere obstacle avoidance: h = |p_i - c_k| - r_i - R_k - margin for each
    robot sphere i in sphere_idxs and obstacle k

    Args:
        robot (Robot): Robot, with collision data
        obstacles (SphereObstacles): Obstacles. Their count K is fixed
        sphere_idxs (ArrayLike | None): Robot collision spheres to check.
            Defaults to all
        ref_key (str | None): If set, ref[ref_key] replaces `obstacles` each step
        max_rows (int | None): If set, keep only this many closest pairs per step
        gain (float): CBF gain (1/s)
        penalty (float): Relaxation penalty
        margin (float): Safety distance from every obstacle
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        robot: Robot,
        obstacles: SphereObstacles,
        sphere_idxs: ArrayLike | None = None,
        ref_key: str | None = None,
        max_rows: int | None = None,
        gain: float = 10.0,
        penalty: float = DEFAULT_PENALTY,
        margin: float = 0.0,
    ):
        super().__init__(robot, gain, penalty)
        self.margin = margin
        self.obstacles = SphereObstacles(
            np.asarray(obstacles.centers, dtype=float),
            np.asarray(obstacles.radii, dtype=float),
            np.asarray(obstacles.active, dtype=bool),
        )
        self.num_obstacles = self.obstacles.radii.shape[0]
        self.sphere_idxs = (
            np.arange(len(self.radii))
            if sphere_idxs is None
            else np.asarray(sphere_idxs)
        )
        self.row_spheres = np.tile(self.sphere_idxs, self.num_obstacles)
        self.ref_key = ref_key
        self._set_num_rows(len(self.row_spheres), max_rows)

    def rows(self, q, ref):
        obstacles = self.obstacles if self.ref_key is None else ref[self.ref_key]
        assert obstacles.radii.shape == (self.num_obstacles,), (
            "Obstacle count must match the constructor"
        )
        joint_tfs = self.robot.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        pos = self.robot._link_collision_positions(joint_tfs)
        idxs = self.sphere_idxs
        delta = (pos[idxs][None] - obstacles.centers[:, None]).reshape(-1, 3)
        offsets = self.radii[idxs][None] + obstacles.radii[:, None] + self.margin
        offsets = offsets.reshape(-1)
        active = jnp.repeat(obstacles.active, len(idxs))
        dist = jnp.linalg.norm(delta, axis=-1)
        h = jnp.where(active, dist - offsets, _INACTIVE_DISTANCE)
        keep = self._keep(h)
        spheres = jnp.asarray(self.row_spheres)[keep]
        Jv, Jw = self.robot._joint_jacobians(joint_tfs)
        J = self.robot._link_collision_jacobians(joint_tfs, Jv, Jw, spheres)
        normals = delta[keep] / dist[keep, None]
        dh = jnp.einsum("ki,kij->kj", normals, J)
        dh = jnp.where(active[keep, None], dh, 0.0)
        return -dh, self.gain * h[keep]

@jax.tree_util.register_static
class Retargeter:
    """Differential IK-based motion retargeter.

    Given a sequence of frames, this class solves for the robot
    configurations q, based on the input DiffIKSolver

    As opposed to just using a DiffIK solver, this adds logic for
    converging to an initial configuration on the first step, and
    processing a whole sequence in a single scan

    Args:
        solver (DiffIKSolver): Diff IK solver
        preprocess (Callable): Input frame -> the solver's reference
        initial_q (Callable): First input frame -> initial guess for q
        converge_max_iters (int): Max iterations to converge onto the first frame
        converge_dt (float | None): Largest convergence stepsize. Defaults to
            1 / solver.max_gain (full Gauss-Newton step)
        converge_tol (float): Convergence tolerance on max |v|
        global_ik_init (GlobalIKSolver | None): If set, solves the first frame by
            global IK before converging, to avoid poor local solutions.
        global_ik_seed (int): Seed for the global IK samples
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        solver: DiffIKSolver,
        preprocess: Callable[[Any], Any],
        initial_q: Callable[[Any], Array],
        converge_max_iters: int = 300,
        converge_dt: float | None = None,
        converge_tol: float = 1e-3,
        global_ik_init: GlobalIKSolver | None = None,
        global_ik_seed: int = 0,
    ):
        self.solver = solver
        self.preprocess = preprocess
        self.initial_q = initial_q
        self.converge_max_iters = converge_max_iters
        if converge_dt is None:
            assert solver.max_gain is not None, "A term has no gain: pass converge_dt"
            converge_dt = 1.0 / solver.max_gain
        self.converge_dt = converge_dt
        self.converge_tol = converge_tol
        self.global_ik_init = global_ik_init
        self.global_ik_seed = global_ik_seed

    def init(self, frame: Any) -> tuple[SolverState, Array]:
        """Converge onto the first frame

        Returns:
            state (SolverState): Converged state
            iters (Array): Number of iterations
        """
        q, ref = self.initial_q(frame), self.preprocess(frame)
        if self.global_ik_init is not None:
            key = jax.random.key(self.global_ik_seed)
            q = self.global_ik_init.solve(q, ref, key).q
        state, iters = self.solver.converge(
            self.solver.init(q),
            ref,
            self.converge_max_iters,
            self.converge_dt,
            self.converge_tol,
        )
        return state, iters

    def step(
        self, state: SolverState, frame: Any, dt: float
    ) -> tuple[SolverState, SolverInfo]:
        """Take one solver step towards an input frame"""
        state, _, info = self.solver.step(state, self.preprocess(frame), dt)
        return state, info

    @jax.jit
    def retarget_clip(self, frames: Any, dt: float) -> tuple[Array, SolverInfo, Array]:
        """Retarget a full clip of input frames

        Args:
            frames (Any): Input frames, with leading time axis T (any pytree)
            dt (float): Time between frames

        Returns:
            q (Array): Configurations, shape (T, nq)
            infos (SolverInfo): Per-step info, leading dim T - 1
            init_iters (Array): Iterations to converge onto the first frame
        """
        first = jax.tree.map(lambda x: x[0], frames)
        rest = jax.tree.map(lambda x: x[1:], frames)
        init_state, init_iters = self.init(first)

        def scan_step(state, frame):
            state, info = self.step(state, frame, dt)
            return state, (state.q, info)

        _, (q, infos) = jax.lax.scan(scan_step, init_state, rest)
        return jnp.concatenate([init_state.q[None], q]), infos, init_iters

class OfflineRetargeter:
    """Retargets many clips, spread across devices. Clips are padded to a multiple
    of bucket frames, and compiled shapes are cached across calls

    Args:
        retargeter (Retargeter): Retargeter
        dt (float): Time between frames
        bucket (int): Padded clip lengths are multiples of this
        devices ("all" | "default" | Sequence[jax.Device]): Devices to spread the
            clips across. Defaults to "all"
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        retargeter: Retargeter,
        dt: float,
        bucket: int = 1024,
        devices: Literal["all", "default"] | Sequence[jax.Device] = "all",
    ):
        self.devices = _resolve_devices(devices)
        self.bucket = bucket
        self.retarget = jax.jit(
            device_vmap(
                lambda clip: retargeter.retarget_clip(clip, dt)[0], self.devices
            )
        )
        self.compiled = {}
        self.compile_time = 0.0

    def __call__(self, clips: Sequence) -> list[np.ndarray]:
        """Retarget clips

        Args:
            clips (Sequence): Clips of input frames, each a pytree with leading
                time axis T. T may differ between clips

        Returns:
            list[np.ndarray]: Configurations, one array per clip, each shape
                (T, nq) with that clip's T
        """
        if not clips:
            return []
        # No more devices than clips, so no device solves a filler clip
        n = min(len(self.devices), len(clips))
        lengths = [len(jax.tree.leaves(clip)[0]) for clip in clips]
        order = sorted(range(len(clips)), key=lambda i: -lengths[i])
        groups = [order[i : i + n] for i in range(0, len(order), n)]
        pending = []
        for group in groups:
            length = -(-lengths[group[0]] // self.bucket) * self.bucket
            # Top up the last group so it shares the compiled shape
            members = [clips[i] for i in group] + [clips[group[0]]] * (n - len(group))
            batch = jax.tree.map(
                lambda *x: np.stack(x),
                *[_pad_with_last_frame(clip, length) for clip in members],
            )
            leaves, structure = jax.tree.flatten(batch)
            key = (structure, tuple(x.shape for x in leaves))
            if key not in self.compiled:
                start = time.perf_counter()
                self.compiled[key] = self.retarget.lower(batch).compile()
                self.compile_time += time.perf_counter() - start
            # Asynchronous dispatch
            pending.append(self.compiled[key](batch))
        qs = [None] * len(clips)
        for group, q in zip(groups, pending):
            q = np.asarray(q)
            for k, i in enumerate(group):
                qs[i] = q[k, : lengths[i]]
        return qs

class OnlineRetargeter:
    """Stateful retargeting wrapper for online operation.

    Call compile() before any strict real-time operation to
    compile the performance-critical methods.
    """

    def __init__(self, retargeter: Retargeter):
        self.retargeter = retargeter
        self.state = None
        self._init = jax.jit(retargeter.init)
        self._step = jax.jit(retargeter.step)

    def compile(self, example_frame: Any) -> None:
        """Compile the init and step functions ahead of time

        Args:
            example_frame (Any): Example input frame (may be jax.ShapeDtypeStructs)
        """
        state, _ = jax.eval_shape(self._init, example_frame)
        self._init.lower(example_frame).compile()
        self._step.lower(state, example_frame, 0.0).compile()

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.state = None

    def step(self, frame: Any, dt: float) -> Array:
        if self.state is None:
            self.state, _ = self._init(frame)
        else:
            self.state, _ = self._step(self.state, frame, float(dt))
        return self.state.q

@jax.tree_util.register_static
class GlobalIKSolver:
    """Multi-start SQP global IK solver


    Args:
        solver (DiffIKSolver): Diff IK solver
        num_samples (int): Number of starts, including q
        q_min, q_max (ArrayLike | "robot"): Sampling range for the actuated
            joints. Default to "robot", for the robot's joint limits, narrowed
            to those of any JointLimits constraints in the solver
        max_iters (int): Max convergence iterations per start
        dt_max (float | None): Largest convergence stepsize. Defaults to
            1 / solver.max_gain
        tol (float): Convergence tolerance on max |v|
        cost_tol (float | None): Cost tolerance for acceptable solutions. If
            this term is set, then we return the closest sampled solution that is
            within cost_tol of the lowest cost. Defaults to None (select the lowest
            cost regardless of how far the solution is in configuration space)
        devices ("all" | "default" | Sequence[jax.Device]): Devices to parallelize
            the samples across. Defaults to "default" (JAX's default device).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        solver: DiffIKSolver,
        num_samples: int = 32,
        q_min: ArrayLike | Literal["robot"] = "robot",
        q_max: ArrayLike | Literal["robot"] = "robot",
        max_iters: int = 200,
        dt_max: float | None = None,
        tol: float = 1e-4,
        cost_tol: float | None = None,
        devices: Literal["all", "default"] | Sequence[jax.Device] = "default",
    ):
        self.solver = solver
        self.num_samples = num_samples

        # Handle joint limits for determining a sampling range
        lower = np.asarray(solver.robot.actuated_joint_lower_limits, dtype=float)
        upper = np.asarray(solver.robot.actuated_joint_upper_limits, dtype=float)
        for c in solver.constraints:
            if isinstance(c, JointLimits):
                lower = np.maximum(lower, c.q_min)
                upper = np.minimum(upper, c.q_max)
        for x in (q_min, q_max):
            if isinstance(x, str):
                assert x == "robot", (
                    f'Sampling limits must be arrays or "robot", got {x!r}'
                )
        self.q_min = lower if isinstance(q_min, str) else np.asarray(q_min, dtype=float)
        self.q_max = upper if isinstance(q_max, str) else np.asarray(q_max, dtype=float)
        assert np.all(np.isfinite(self.q_min)) and np.all(np.isfinite(self.q_max)), (
            "Unbounded sampling range: pass q_min and q_max, or give the solver "
            + "JointLimits"
        )

        self.max_iters = max_iters
        if dt_max is None:
            assert solver.max_gain is not None, "A term has no gain: pass dt_max"
            dt_max = 1.0 / solver.max_gain
        self.dt_max = dt_max
        self.tol = tol
        self.cost_tol = cost_tol
        self.devices = tuple(_resolve_devices(devices))

    def solve(self, q: Array, ref: Any, key: Array) -> GlobalIKResult:
        """Solve global IK

        Args:
            q (Array): Current configuration, shape (nq,)
            ref (Any): Reference data (any pytree)
            key (Array): PRNG key for the samples

        Returns:
            GlobalIKResult: Result
        """
        solver, robot = self.solver, self.solver.robot
        joints = slice(robot.nq_floating, None)

        def converge(q0, ref):
            state, iters = solver.converge(
                solver.init(q0), ref, self.max_iters, self.dt_max, self.tol
            )
            return state.q, iters, solver.cost(state.q, ref)

        def select(qs, costs, iters, sampled):
            if self.cost_tol is None:
                best = jnp.argmin(costs)
            else:
                acceptable = costs <= jnp.min(costs) + self.cost_tol
                distance = jnp.sum((qs[:, joints] - q[joints]) ** 2, axis=1)
                best = jnp.argmin(jnp.where(acceptable, distance, jnp.inf))
            return GlobalIKResult(qs[best], costs[best], qs, costs, iters, sampled)

        def sample():
            q0s = sample_configurations(
                robot, q, key, self.num_samples, self.q_min, self.q_max
            )
            converge_all = device_vmap(converge, self.devices, in_axes=(0, None))
            qs, iters, costs = converge_all(q0s, ref)
            return select(qs, costs, iters, jnp.array(True))

        if self.cost_tol is None:
            return sample()
        q_local, iters_local, cost_local = converge(q, ref)

        def keep_local():
            tile = lambda x: jnp.broadcast_to(x, (self.num_samples,) + jnp.shape(x))
            return select(
                tile(q_local), tile(cost_local), tile(iters_local), jnp.array(False)
            )

        return jax.lax.cond(cost_local <= self.cost_tol, keep_local, sample)

def sample_configurations(
    robot: Robot,
    q: Array,
    key: Array,
    num_samples: int,
    q_min: ArrayLike | Literal["robot"] = "robot",
    q_max: ArrayLike | Literal["robot"] = "robot",
) -> Array:
    """Sample configurations for global IK

    The actuated joints are sampled uniformly. The floating base stays at q's:
    it has no joint limits to sample within, and is usually pinned by a task

    Args:
        robot (Robot): Robot model
        q (Array): Nominal configuration, shape (nq,).
            This is also included as the first sample
        key (Array): PRNG key
        num_samples (int): Number of samples, including q
        q_min (ArrayLike | "robot"): Lower joint bounds, shape (num_actuated,).
            Defaults to "robot", for robot.actuated_joint_lower_limits
        q_max (ArrayLike | "robot"): Upper joint bounds, shape (num_actuated,).
            Defaults to "robot", for robot.actuated_joint_upper_limits

    Returns:
        Array: Sampled configurations, shape (num_samples, nq)
    """
    if isinstance(q_min, str):
        assert q_min == "robot", f'q_min must be an array or "robot", got {q_min!r}'
        q_min = np.asarray(robot.actuated_joint_lower_limits, dtype=float)
        assert np.all(np.isfinite(q_min)), "Unbounded joint limits: pass q_min"
    if isinstance(q_max, str):
        assert q_max == "robot", f'q_max must be an array or "robot", got {q_max!r}'
        q_max = np.asarray(robot.actuated_joint_upper_limits, dtype=float)
        assert np.all(np.isfinite(q_max)), "Unbounded joint limits: pass q_max"
    joints = jax.random.uniform(
        key,
        (num_samples - 1, robot.nq - robot.nq_floating),
        minval=q_min,
        maxval=q_max,
        dtype=q.dtype,
    )
    base = jnp.broadcast_to(
        q[: robot.nq_floating], (num_samples - 1, robot.nq_floating)
    )
    return jnp.concatenate([q[None], jnp.concatenate([base, joints], axis=1)])

def load_bvh(
    filepath: str | Path, to_world: ArrayLike | None = None, scale: float = 0.01
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, list[str]]:
    """Global bone poses from a BVH file

    Args:
        filepath (str | Path): BVH file
        to_world (ArrayLike | None): Rotation from the BVH frame to the world,
            shape (3, 3). Defaults to identity
        scale (float): BVH length unit (m). Defaults to cm

    Returns:
        poses (np.ndarray): Poses [position, WXYZ quaternion], shape (T, B, 7)
        names (list[str]): The B bone names

    Raises:
        ValueError: If any frame has NaNs
    """
    names, parents, local_pos, local_rot = _parse_bvh(filepath)
    T, B = local_pos.shape[:2]
    rot = np.zeros((T, B, 3, 3))
    pos = np.zeros((T, B, 3))
    for i, parent in enumerate(parents):  # Parents precede their children
        if parent < 0:
            rot[:, i], pos[:, i] = local_rot[:, i], local_pos[:, i]
        else:
            rot[:, i] = rot[:, parent] @ local_rot[:, i]
            pos[:, i] = pos[:, parent] + np.einsum(
                "tij,tj->ti", rot[:, parent], local_pos[:, i]
            )
    to_world = np.eye(3) if to_world is None else np.asarray(to_world, dtype=float)
    pos = scale * pos @ to_world.T
    quat = Rotation.from_matrix((to_world @ rot).reshape(-1, 3, 3))
    quat = quat.as_quat(scalar_first=True).reshape(T, B, 4)
    return np.concatenate([pos, quat], axis=-1), names

def smooth_poses(
    poses: ArrayLike, dt: float, sigma_pos: float = 0.0, sigma_rot: float = 0.0
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Zero-phase Gaussian smoothing of a clip of poses along time,
    for offline retargeting

    Args:
        poses (ArrayLike): Poses [position, WXYZ quaternion], shape (T, ..., 7)
        dt (float): Time between poses
        sigma_pos (float): Position kernel standard deviation (s). 0 to not smooth
        sigma_rot (float): Rotation kernel standard deviation (s). 0 to not smooth

    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Smoothed poses, shape (T, ..., 7)
    """
    poses = np.array(poses, dtype=float)
    if sigma_pos > 0:
        poses[..., :3] = gaussian_filter1d(
            poses[..., :3], sigma_pos / dt, axis=0, mode="nearest"
        )
    if sigma_rot > 0:
        quat = poses[..., 3:]
        # Sign-align, so componentwise filtering approximates the geodesic mean
        flips = np.sum(quat[1:] * quat[:-1], axis=-1) < 0
        signs = np.cumprod(np.where(flips, -1.0, 1.0), axis=0)
        quat[1:] *= signs[..., None]
        quat = gaussian_filter1d(quat, sigma_rot / dt, axis=0, mode="nearest")
        poses[..., 3:] = quat / np.linalg.norm(quat, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    return poses

def resample_poses(poses: ArrayLike, fps_in: float, fps_out: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Resample a clip of poses to a new frame rate

    Args:
        poses (ArrayLike): Poses [position, WXYZ quaternion], shape (T, ..., 7)
        fps_in (float): Frame rate of poses
        fps_out (float): Frame rate to resample to

    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Resampled poses, shape (T_out, ..., 7), with
            T_out = floor((T - 1) * fps_out / fps_in) + 1
    """
    poses = np.asarray(poses, dtype=float)
    T = len(poses)
    assert T >= 2, "Need at least two poses to resample"
    flat = poses.reshape(T, -1, 7)
    n = flat.shape[1]

    T_out = int(np.floor((T - 1) * fps_out / fps_in + 1e-9)) + 1
    frame_times = np.arange(T_out) * fps_in / fps_out  # In input frames
    i = np.minimum(frame_times.astype(int), T - 2)
    alpha = frame_times - i
    before, after = flat[i], flat[i + 1]

    a = alpha[:, None, None]
    pos = (1 - a) * before[..., :3] + a * after[..., :3]

    rot_before = Rotation.from_quat(before[..., 3:].reshape(-1, 4), scalar_first=True)
    rot_after = Rotation.from_quat(after[..., 3:].reshape(-1, 4), scalar_first=True)
    relative = (rot_before.inv() * rot_after).as_rotvec()
    a = np.repeat(alpha, n)[:, None]
    rot = rot_before * Rotation.from_rotvec(a * relative)
    quat = rot.as_quat(scalar_first=True).reshape(T_out, n, 4)

    out = np.concatenate([pos, quat], axis=-1)
    return out.reshape(T_out, *poses.shape[1:])

def save_motion(path: str | Path, robot: Robot, q: ArrayLike, fps: float) -> None:
    """Save a motion as an .npz file with fields q (float32), fps, and the
    actuated joint_names

    Args:
        path (str | Path): Output file (.npz)
        robot (Robot): Robot model
        q (ArrayLike): Configurations, shape (T, nq)
        fps (float): Frame rate
    """
    q = np.asarray(q)
    assert q.ndim == 2 and q.shape[1] == robot.nq, (
        f"q has shape {q.shape}, expected (T, {robot.nq})"
    )
    np.savez(
        path,
        q=q.astype(np.float32),
        fps=float(fps),
        joint_names=np.array(robot.joint_names[robot.nv_floating :]),
    )

@jax.tree_util.register_static
class Manipulator(Robot):
    """Manipulator kinematics and dynamics

    Args:
        urdf_filename (str): Path to the URDF file to load
        collision_data (Optional[dict]): Collision information. Contains info
            on body/root collision data, as well as self-collision pairs.
            See collision_utils for more detail. Defaults to None.
        joint_ordering (Optional[list[str]]): A specific joint ordering to use.
            Defaults to None (infer ordering from URDF)
        floating_base (Optional[str]): How to model a free-floating base: None (fixed base),
            "quaternion", or "euler". See Robot for details. Defaults to None.
        ee_offset (Optional[ArrayLike]): Transformation matrix specifying the end-effector
            offset from the last joint frame. Defaults to None.
        default_configuration (Optional[ArrayLike]): The default configuration, shape (nq,).
            See Robot for details. Defaults to None (identity base pose, all joints at zero)
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        urdf_filename: str,
        collision_data: dict | None = None,
        joint_ordering: list[str] | None = None,
        floating_base: str | None = None,
        ee_offset: ArrayLike | None = None,
        default_configuration: ArrayLike | None = None,
    ):
        super().__init__(
            urdf_filename,
            collision_data,
            joint_ordering,
            floating_base=floating_base,
            default_configuration=default_configuration,
        )
        # TODO decide if floating base should be an input? Only makes sense for in-space manipulators...
        assert self.is_pure_kinematic_chain

        # TODO REORGANIZE ALL OF THIS BELOW
        self.ee_parent_chain = np.arange(self.nv)

        if ee_offset is None:
            ee_offset = np.eye(4)
        else:
            ee_offset = np.asarray(ee_offset, dtype=float)
            assert ee_offset.shape == (4, 4)
            ee_offset = ee_offset

        self.ee_offset = ee_offset

    # EE STUFF

    def ee_transform(self, q: Array) -> Array:
        """Transformation matrix of the end effector (EE frame --> world frame)

        Args:
            q (Array): Configuration vector, shape (nq,)

        Returns:
            Array: Transformation matrix, shape (4, 4)
        """
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._ee_transform(transforms)

    def _ee_transform(self, joint_transforms: Array) -> Array:
        """Helper function: Compute EE transform given joint transforms"""
        parent_index = self.ee_parent_chain[-1]
        return self._frame_transform(joint_transforms, self.ee_offset, parent_index)

    def ee_jacobian(self, q: Array) -> Array:
        """Jacobian [Jv; Jw] of the end effector given the joint configuration

        Args:
            q (Array): Configuration vector, shape (nq,)

        Returns:
            Array: Jacobian, shape (6, nv). The first 3 rows are the linear Jacobian,
                and the last 3 rows are the angular Jacobian
        """
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._ee_jacobian(transforms)

    def _ee_jacobian(self, joint_transforms: Array):
        """Helper function: Compute EE jacobian given joint transforms"""
        return self._frame_jacobian(
            joint_transforms, self.ee_offset, self.ee_parent_chain
        )

    def ee_jacobian_and_derivative(self, q: Array, v: Array) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """End-effector Jacobian and its time derivative (w.r.t world)

        Args:
            q (Array): Configuration vector, shape (nq,)
            v (Array): Generalized velocities, shape (nv,)

        Returns:
            J (Array): EE Jacobian, shape (6, nv)
            Jdot (Array): Time derivative of the EE Jacobian, shape (6, nv)
        """
        transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._ee_jacobian_and_derivative(v, transforms)

    def _ee_jacobian_and_derivative(
        self, v: Array, joint_transforms: Array
    ) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Helper function: Compute EE Jacobian and time derivative given joint transforms"""
        return self._frame_jacobian_and_derivative(
            v, joint_transforms, self.ee_offset, self.ee_parent_chain
        )

    def ee_manipulability_index(self, q: Array) -> float:
        """Manipulability index of the end-effector Jacobian

        Args:
            q (Array): Configuration vector, shape (nq,)

        Returns:
            float: Manipulability index
        """
        joint_transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        return self._ee_manipulability_index(joint_transforms)

    def _ee_manipulability_index(self, joint_transforms: Array) -> float:
        """Helper function: Computes EE manipulability index given joint transforms"""
        J_full = self._ee_jacobian(joint_transforms)
        return self._manipulability_index_helper(J_full, self.ee_parent_chain)

    def torque_control_matrices(
        self, q: Array, v: Array
    ) -> tuple[Array, Array, Array, Array, Array, Array]:
        """Compute the matrices required for operational space torque control
        with just a single evaluation of the kinematics

        Args:
            q (Array): Configuration vector, shape (nq,)
            v (Array): Generalized velocities, shape (nv,)

        Returns:
            M (Array): Mass matrix, shape (nv, nv)
            M_inv (Array): Inverse of the mass matrix, shape (nv, nv)
            G (Array): Gravity vector, shape (nv,)
            C (Array): Centrifugal/coriolis vector, shape (nv,)
            J (Array): End effector basic Jacobian, shape (6, nv)
            T (Array): End effector transformation matrix, shape (4, 4)
        """
        joint_transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        M = self._mass_matrix(joint_transforms)
        M_inv = self.mass_matrix_inverse(M)
        G = self._gravity_vector(joint_transforms)
        C = self._centrifugal_coriolis_vector(v, joint_transforms)
        J = self._ee_jacobian(joint_transforms)
        T = self._ee_transform(joint_transforms)
        return M, M_inv, G, C, J, T

    def velocity_control_matrices(self, q: Array) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Compute the matrices required for operational space velocity control
        with just a single evaluation of the kinematics

        Args:
            q (Array): Configuration vector, shape (nq,)

        Returns:
            J (Array): End effector basic Jacobian, shape (6, nv)
            T (Array): End effector transformation matrix, shape (4, 4)
        """
        joint_transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        J = self._ee_jacobian(joint_transforms)
        T = self._ee_transform(joint_transforms)
        return J, T

    def dynamically_consistent_velocity_control_matrices(
        self, q: Array
    ) -> tuple[Array, Array, Array]:
        """Compute the matrices required for operational space velocity control
        with just a single evaluation of the kinematics.

        This version also returns the inverse of the mass matrix, which is required
        to construct the dynamically-consistent generalized Jacobian inverse

        Args:
            q (Array): Configuration vector, shape (nq,)

        Returns:
            M_inv (Array): Inverse of the mass matrix, shape (nv, nv)
            J (Array): End effector basic Jacobian, shape (6, nv)
            T (Array): End effector transformation matrix, shape (4, 4)
        """
        joint_transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
        J = self._ee_jacobian(joint_transforms)
        T = self._ee_transform(joint_transforms)
        M = self._mass_matrix(joint_transforms)
        M_inv = self.mass_matrix_inverse(M)
        return M_inv, J, T

    """Compute the matrices required for operational space velocity control
    with just a single evaluation of the kinematics.

    This version also returns the inverse of the mass matrix, which is required
    to construct the dynamically-consistent generalized Jacobian inverse

    Args:
        q (Array): Configuration vector, shape (nq,)

    Returns:
        M_inv (Array): Inverse of the mass matrix, shape (nv, nv)
        J (Array): End effector basic Jacobian, shape (6, nv)
        T (Array): End effector transformation matrix, shape (4, 4)
    """
    joint_transforms = self.joint_to_world_transforms(q)
    J = self._ee_jacobian(joint_transforms)
    T = self._ee_transform(joint_transforms)
    M = self._mass_matrix(joint_transforms)
    M_inv = self.mass_matrix_inverse(M)
    return M_inv, J, T

def integrate(self, q: Array, v: Array, dt: float) -> Array:
    """Integrates a configuration forward in time with a constant velocity

    Args:
        q (Array): Configuration, shape (nq,)
        v (Array): Velocity, shape (nv,)
        dt (float): Timestep

    Returns:
        Array: New configuration, shape (nq,)
    """
    if not self.is_quaternion_base:
        return q + v * dt
    pos = q[:3] + v[:3] * dt
    quat = quat_wxyz_multiply(q[3:7], quat_wxyz_exp(v[3:6] * dt))
    quat = quat / jnp.linalg.norm(quat)
    q_act = q[7:] + v[6:] * dt
    return jnp.concatenate([pos, quat, q_act])

def velocity_to_qdot_map(self, q: Array) -> Array:
    """Matrix E(q) mapping velocities to the time derivative of the configuration:
    q_dot = E(q) @ v

    This is useful when combining autodiff w.r.t. q with velocities, e.g.
    dh/dt = (dh/dq) @ E(q) @ v. When nq == nv, this is the identity.

    Args:
        q (Array): Configuration, shape (nq,)

    Returns:
        Array: Velocity map, shape (nq, nv)
    """
    if not self.is_quaternion_base:
        return jnp.eye(self.nv)
    w, x, y, z = q[3:7]
    # q_dot = 0.5 * quat * [0, omega_body] (quaternion multiplication)
    quat_map = 0.5 * jnp.array([[-x, -y, -z], [w, -z, y], [z, w, -x], [-y, x, w]])
    E = jnp.zeros((self.nq, self.nv))
    E = E.at[:3, :3].set(jnp.eye(3))
    E = E.at[3:7, 3:6].set(quat_map)
    E = E.at[7:, 6:].set(jnp.eye(self.num_actuated_joints))
    return E

    """Quadruped kinematics and dynamics

    Args:
        urdf_filename (str): Path to the URDF file to load
        front_left_foot_parent_joint_name (str): Name of the front left foot's parent joint
        front_right_foot_parent_joint_name (str): Name of the front right foot's parent joint
        hind_left_foot_parent_joint_name (str): Name of the hind left foot's parent joint
        hind_right_foot_parent_joint_name (str): Name of the hind right foot's parent joint

            left foot offset from the parent joint frame. Defaults to None.
        front_right_foot_offset (Optional[ArrayLike]): Transformation matrix specifying the front
            right foot offset from the parent joint frame. Defaults to None.
        hind_left_foot_offset (Optional[ArrayLike]): Transformation matrix specifying the hind
            left foot offset from the parent joint frame. Defaults to None.
        hind_right_foot_offset (Optional[ArrayLike]): Transformation matrix specifying the hind
            right foot offset from the parent joint frame. Defaults to None.
        collision_data (Optional[dict]): Collision information. Contains info

        default_configuration (Optional[ArrayLike]): The default configuration, shape (nq,).
            See Robot for details. Defaults to None (identity base pose, all joints at zero)

        self,
        urdf_filename,
        front_left_foot_parent_joint_name: str,
        front_right_foot_parent_joint_name: str,
        hind_left_foot_parent_joint_name: str,
        hind_right_foot_parent_joint_name: str,

        front_right_foot_offset: ArrayLike | None = None,
        hind_left_foot_offset: ArrayLike | None = None,
        hind_right_foot_offset: ArrayLike | None = None,
        collision_data: dict | None = None,
        joint_ordering: list[str] | None = None,
        floating_base: str | None = "quaternion",
        default_configuration: ArrayLike | None = None,
    ):
        super().__init__(
            urdf_filename,
            collision_data,
            joint_ordering,
            floating_base,
            default_configuration,
        )

        self.front_left_foot_parent_chain = np.flatnonzero(
            self.ancestor_mask[
                self.joint_name_to_index[front_left_foot_parent_joint_name]

            self.ancestor_mask[

def integrate(self, q: Array, v: Array, dt: float) -> Array:
    """Integrates a configuration forward in time with a constant velocity

    Args:
        q (Array): Configuration, shape (nq,)
        v (Array): Velocity, shape (nv,)
        dt (float): Timestep

    Returns:
        Array: New configuration, shape (nq,)
    """
    if not self.is_quaternion_base:
        return q + v * dt
    pos = q[:3] + v[:3] * dt
    quat = quat_wxyz_multiply(q[3:7], quat_wxyz_exp(v[3:6] * dt))
    quat = quat / jnp.linalg.norm(quat)
    q_act = q[7:] + v[6:] * dt
    return jnp.concatenate([pos, quat, q_act])
